title: Astela policies
description: A policy file of Astela on Linux, in /etc/astela/policies/managed/ for mandatory or /etc/astela/policies/recommended/ for recommended policies. Written by tools/policies/reference.ts; docs/admin/policies.md describes every policy.

ApplicationLocaleValue.description: The language of the menus, dialogs and pages of the browser: system, or a language code such as en or de. A code without a translation shows English. Unlike in Chromium, a code with a region, such as de-DE, is not valid. Takes effect after a restart.

AuthServerAllowlist.description: The servers that may get the sign-in of the system for integrated authentication, with Kerberos (Negotiate) or NTLM, as a list separated by commas, such as *.example.com,example.com. A * stands for any start of a name. Without the policy, the browser answers such a request only where the system allows it, such as for the Intranet zone on Windows. A change applies at the next read of the policies. Mandatory only. Sensitive: applies only from managed/.

AutoHideToolbar.description: Whether the tabs and the toolbar hide until they are needed, with the tab strip at the top and never in popups. As a mandatory policy, it also keeps the command that turns the hiding on and off from running, and the layout presets of the settings page and the setup guide that would change it cannot be chosen.

AutoUpdateCheckPeriodMinutes.description: The minutes between two automatic checks for updates. Without the policy, the browser checks every 240 minutes. Mandatory only.

BlockThirdPartyCookies.description: Keeps cookies away from requests, responses, frames and workers of other sites than the one of the page. Chromium blocks them from the next start of the browser, with the policies that the last start read. Private windows always block them. Takes effect after a restart.

BookmarkBarEnabled.description: Shows or hides the bookmarks bar.

CommandPaletteEnabled.description: Turns the command palette and tab search on or off. While it is off, their shortcuts reach web pages.

ContentBlockerAllowedSites.description: The sites on which the content blocker is off, by host name or domain, such as intranet.example.com; a domain covers its hosts. Mandatory, the list replaces the one of people and they cannot change it, also not with the switches of the shield and of site information or an import of settings; [] allows no site. Recommended, it is the list that people start from.

ContentBlockerAnnoyancesEnabled.description: Turns the optional list of the content blocker against annoyances on or off.

ContentBlockerCookieNoticesEnabled.description: Turns the optional list of the content blocker against cookie notices on or off.

ContentBlockerEnabled.description: Turns the content blocker on or off.

DefaultBrowserSettingEnabled.description: false keeps people from making the browser their default browser. The setting then says that the organization manages it, and the browser refuses the change. Mandatory only.

DefaultSearchProviderSearchURL.description: The search address of the address bar and the new tab page. An https address with {searchTerms}, as in Chrome, or %s where the search terms go, such as https://search.example.com/search?q={searchTerms}. Chrome's other parameters, such as {inputEncoding}, are not replaced. Mandatory only. Sensitive: applies only from managed/.

DeveloperToolsAvailability.description: 2 keeps the developer tools closed: Inspect in the context menu does nothing, the menus have no Developer tools or grey it out, and F12 and the other keys of the developer tools reach the page. 0 and 1 allow them for web pages, as in Chromium. The pages of the browser itself never get the developer tools. Mandatory only.

DnsOverHttpsMode.description: How the browser looks up the addresses of sites: automatic uses DNS over HTTPS with the services of DnsOverHttpsTemplates or, without them, where the provider of the system offers it; secure only with the services of DnsOverHttpsTemplates; off never. secure without a service works like automatic. Mandatory only. Sensitive: applies only from managed/.

DnsOverHttpsTemplates.description: The DNS over HTTPS services that DnsOverHttpsMode uses: https:// URI templates, separated by spaces. Templates that Chromium would refuse, such as ones with unbalanced braces or a variable in the host, are not valid. Mandatory only. Sensitive: applies only from managed/.

DownloadDirectory.description: The folder where downloads are saved; empty for the downloads folder of the system. The browser replaces ${user_name} and ${machine_name}, as Chrome does on Linux, such as in /home/${user_name}/Downloads. It refuses the value with any other variable, such as ${user_home} or the variables of Chrome on Windows and macOS (${documents}, ${users}).

HomepageLocation.description: The page of the home button and of its shortcut, as an http or https address; empty for the new tab page. An address without a scheme, such as intranet.example.com, gets https://.

HttpAllowlist.description: Hosts that HTTPS-First leaves on their insecure address, such as intranet.example.com. [*.]example.com and *.example.com also name every host below example.com. IP addresses, names without a dot and names that end in .localhost, .local, .internal, .lan, .home.arpa, .test, .example, .invalid are never upgraded and need no entry. Mandatory only.

HttpsOnlyMode.description: Whether HTTPS-First loads sites over HTTPS and warns before an insecure connection: disallowed turns it off, force_enabled and force_balanced_enabled keep it on. The browser has one mode, so both values that keep it on do the same. Chrome's allowed, which leaves the choice to people, is not valid. Mandatory only.

ImportEnabled.description: false turns off the import from other browsers, on the settings page and in the setup guide. Mandatory only.

PictureInPictureEnabled.description: Turns the picture in picture of the browser on or off: its button next to the address bar and its menu items. A video that shows in picture in picture stays there, and pages that offer picture in picture themselves keep it.

PrivateModeAvailability.description: 1 keeps people from opening private windows; 0 allows them. With 1, the menus have no New private window or grey it out, and its shortcut reaches the page. Chrome's 2, which makes every window private, is not supported and not valid. Mandatory only.

PromptForDownloadLocation.description: Whether the browser asks where to save each download.

ProxyBypassList.description: The hosts that ProxyMode fixed_servers reaches without the proxy, separated by commas, such as *.intranet.example.com,192.168.0.0/16. Chromium's format: a * stands for any start of a name, <local> for names without a dot, and an address with / for a range of IP addresses. localhost and the loopback addresses never go through the proxy. Mandatory only. Sensitive: applies only from managed/.

ProxyMode.description: How the browser finds its proxy: direct uses none, system the settings of the system, auto_detect looks for a proxy script in the network (WPAD), fixed_servers uses ProxyServer, and pac_script the script at ProxyPacUrl. As in Chrome, the other proxy policies count only in the modes that use them: ProxyServer and ProxyBypassList with fixed_servers, ProxyPacUrl with pac_script. fixed_servers without ProxyServer and pac_script without ProxyPacUrl set no proxy; then, as without ProxyMode, the browser uses the settings of the system or the switches it was started with. A value that does nothing is logged as Policy value has no effect. A change applies to every window, private windows and workspaces that keep their data apart included, at the next read of the policies, and closes the open connections. Chrome's ProxySettings is not supported. Mandatory only. Sensitive: applies only from managed/.

ProxyPacUrl.description: The address of the proxy script (PAC file) of ProxyMode pac_script, such as https://wpad.example.com/proxy.pac. A data: address that holds the script works too; a local file does not, as in Chrome. Mandatory only. Sensitive: applies only from managed/.

ProxyServer.description: The proxy of ProxyMode fixed_servers, as host:port or as an address such as http://proxy.example.com:3128 or socks5://proxy.example.com:1080. Chromium's rules for each scheme work too, such as http=proxy1:80;https=proxy2:443. Mandatory only. Sensitive: applies only from managed/.

ReaderViewEnabled.description: Turns the reader view on or off. While it is off, the browser checks no page for an article.

RestoreOnStartup.description: What the browser opens when it starts, with Chromium's numbers: 1 the last session, 4 the pages of RestoreOnStartupURLs, 5 a new tab page. After the browser did not quit normally, as after a crash, it brings the last session back; only a mandatory RestoreOnStartup keeps the start to its value then, as on shared computers.

RestoreOnStartupURLs.description: The pages that open at the start when RestoreOnStartup is 4, in this order. An address without a scheme, such as intranet.example.com, gets https://. As in Chrome, the value is a list, also for one page.

SetupGuideEnabled.description: false keeps the setup guide from opening on the first start of a profile. Starting the browser with --no-first-run does the same for one start. Mandatory only.

ShowHomeButton.description: Shows or hides the home button of the toolbar.

SleepingTabsEnabled.description: Whether tabs go to sleep by themselves after they were not used for a while. People can still put a tab to sleep from its menu.

SleepingTabsTimeout.description: How many seconds a tab stays unused before it goes to sleep, with the values of Microsoft Edge.

SplitViewEnabled.description: Turns split view on or off. Off ends the split views that show.

SSLErrorOverrideAllowed.description: false keeps people from continuing to a site whose certificate is not trusted; certificates accepted earlier in the session are refused again. Mandatory only.

TabStripPosition.description: Where the tab strip is: at the top, at the bottom, or on the left or right side.

TargetChannel.description: The update channel. The beta channel also receives the stable releases. A switch from beta to stable never installs an older version; the browser stays on its version until a stable release overtakes it. Mandatory only.

TargetVersionPrefix.description: Installs only versions that start with this prefix, such as 0.1: the highest version of the feed that matches. Mandatory only.

ToolbarPlacement.description: Whether the address bar has a row of its own below the tabs (own-row) or shares the row of the tabs (tab-row). It applies only with the tab strip at the top.

UpdatePolicy.description: How the browser updates itself: 0 not at all, 1 by itself, 2 only when people ask for it. With 2, people check for updates in About, which also shows the state of the updates. A change applies at once: 0 stops the checks, cancels a download that runs and drops an update that is ready. Installations that the system or IT updates, such as the deb, rpm and MSI packages, never update themselves. Mandatory only.

UpdateURL.description: The address of an organization mirror of the update feed, instead of the website of the project. The browser reads updates/v1/index.json and updates/v1/releases/<version>.json below this address and checks their signatures as on the website. Mandatory only. Sensitive: applies only from managed/.

URLAllowlist.description: The exceptions of URLBlocklist, as filters of the same format, such as mail.example.com with a blocklist of *. Of the filters of both lists that match an address, the most specific decides: * counts least, a host with a leading . more than one with its subdomains, then the longer host, the longer path and the more parameters of the query; on a tie, the allowlist wins. The first 1000 entries count. Mandatory only.

URLBlocklist.description: The addresses that pages and frames may not open, as filters such as example.com; such a tab says that the organization blocks the site. Chrome's filter format, [scheme://][.]host[:port][/path][?query]: a host also blocks its subdomains unless it starts with ., * blocks every address, https://* every address of a scheme and *:8080 a port; a path blocks the addresses that start with it, and ?key=value those with that parameter, with a final * for the start of a value. file:///home/ blocks the local files below a folder, and on Windows file:///C:/Users/, also written with a lower-case drive or with \. As in Chrome, the first 1000 entries count; entries that are no filters and those after the 1000th are ignored and logged as Policy entries ignored with their positions. The browser's own pages are never blocked, and as in Chrome, * does not block the internal pages of Chromium, such as its PDF viewer and the developer tools, which chrome-extension://* and devtools://* block. A change applies to the next pages that load, at the next read of the policies. Mandatory only.

WorkspacesEnabled.description: Turns workspaces on or off. Off shows the tabs of all workspaces of a window together; the workspaces come back when the policy turns them on again.
